title: CUrator: An Efficient LLM Execution Engine with Optimized Integration of CUDA Libraries
problem: Modern LLMs require optimal GEMM performance on diverse GPUs; existing CUTLASS and cuBLAS libraries offer tuning but lack systematic exploration of LLM-specific parameters and multi-GPU optimization strategies.
motivation: GEMM is the bottleneck in LLM inference; finding optimal CUDA library mapping (CUTLASS vs cuBLAS) and kernels across LLMs and GPU types requires systematic search.
method: CUrator generates CUTLASS/cuBLAS-friendly TVM graph IRs for LLMs (BERT, GPT, Llama), performs comprehensive CUTLASS tuning parameter search for each GEMM, introduces Split-K optimizations (reduction key init, batch support), and selects best cuBLAS/CUTLASS path per GEMM.
key_novelty: Systematic CUTLASS parameter tuning integrated into TVM with Split-K support for both Batch and regular GEMMs, combined with dual-path selection (cuBLAS vs CUTLASS).
contributions: CUTLASS/cuBLAS mapping to TVM graph IRs for multiple LLMs
Split-K optimizations for reduction key initialization and batch GEMMs
1.50x and 4.99x inference speedups on A100 GPU in single/half precision
limitations: Evaluation limited to A100; generalization to other NVIDIA GPU types (H100, L40) not discussed.
primary_theme: LLM inference optimization via CUTLASS tuning
